predecessors.name: Mongol Empire
predecessors.text: the Hulaguid ulus: Persia, Iraq, the Caucasus and Anatolia (Cliopatria row ends 1293, Ilkhanate starts 1294)

successors.name: Jalayirid Sultanate
successors.text: Baghdad and Iraq with Azerbaijan; the Abu Said page names the Jalayirids among the successors

successors.name: Chobanids
successors.text: Azerbaijan under the Chupanids ('Little' Hasan took Azerbaijan in 1338, Ilkhanate page)

successors.name: Muzaffarid dynasty
successors.text: Fars and Kerman; named on the Abu Said page

successors.name: Sarbadars
successors.text: Khorasan; named on the Abu Said page

successors.name: Kart dynasty
successors.text: Herat and its surroundings, autonomous under Kart rulers throughout (Ilkhanate page)

successors.name: Injuids
successors.text: Cliopatria row only; no page opened names the Injuids

ledger.x: 1294: the Ilkhanate appears on Cliopatria's map when its Mongol Empire row ends in 1293.
9 December 1295: Duwa of the Chagatai Khanate invades Khorasan.
October 1299: Ghazan invades Syria.
April 1303: the Mongol advance on Syria ends at Marj al-Saffar.
1304: 'general peace among the Mongol khanates'; the Chagatai pressure on Khorasan ends.
1305: direct Ilkhanid control of Sultanate of Rum's land ends on Cliopatria's map.
1305: Rum stays an Ilkhanid vassal.
1305: direct Ilkhanid control of Beylik of Hamid's land ends on Cliopatria's map.

1305: Beylik of Hamid is drawn as an Ilkhanid dependency because the Abu Said page keeps an Ilkhanid governor of Anatolia to 1332 (Timurtash after 1319, Hasan reinstated 1332); no page opened calls Beylik of Hamid a vassal, so this is a reading.

wars.name: Ilkhanate-Chagatai war of Duwa and Qutlugh Khwaja
wars.outcome: Duwa invades Khorasan on 9 December 1295; Ghazan musters about 80,000 troops against Chagatai raiders under Qutlugh Khwaja in 1303; the war ends in the 'general peace among the Mongol khanates' of 1304.

wars.name: Mongol invasions of Syria under Ghazan
wars.outcome: Ghazan takes Aleppo (October 1299), wins at Wadi al-Khazandar (23/24 December 1299), holds Damascus for days (30 December 1299 to 6 January 1300, citadel unbroken), raids again in February 1301 and is defeated at Marj al-Saffar in April 1303.

wars.name: Rebellion of Sulemish in Anatolia
wars.outcome: Sulemish's revolt ends in defeat near Erzincan on 27 April 1299; he is burned at Tabriz on 27 September 1299.

wars.name: Revolt of the emirs against Abu Said
wars.outcome: Irenchin's rebellion is crushed at Zanjan-Rud on 13 July 1319 (Ilkhanate page) and the rebel emirs near Mianeh on 20 June 1319 (Abu Said page); Georgia's governor Qurumishi is executed; the Chagatayid Yasa'ur revolts in 1319 and is killed by Kebek in 1320.

wars.name: Golden Horde invasions of Azerbaijan
wars.outcome: Oz Beg invades Azerbaijan in 1319 with the Chagatayid Yasa'ur, again in the mid-1320s against Chupan and in 1335, when Abu Said dies on the way to meet him in Karabakh.

wars.name: Collapse of the Ilkhanate
wars.outcome: After Abu Said's death the Hulaguid line continues under puppet Ilkhans (Arpa Ke'un 1335-1336, Musa 1336-1337, Muhammad 1336-1338, Sati Beg 1338-1339, Sulayman 1339-1343) while the emirs divide the land; 'Little' Hasan takes Azerbaijan in 1338.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened: the Mamluk frontier on the Euphrates was fixed by war, and the 1322 peace gives no line; the Caucasus, Khorasan and Anatolian frontiers are approximate.
